subject: Clarifications on PHI dataflows and BAA terms for HavenWell
messages:
From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@havenwell.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@havenwell.com>, HavenWell Legal <legal@havenwell.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifications on PHI dataflows and BAA terms for Redwood

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our technical and legal teams reviewed the materials and had a couple of follow-up questions before we share the packet with procurement:

1) We saw in the diagram that transient PHI is routed through a hosted cache layer in the Redwood Hosted API. Can you confirm whether PHI is ever written to persistent storage in the hosted offering, and if so under what conditions?

2) Encryption at rest: do you manage the keys for hosted customers or do you offer a BYOK/KMS integration? If managed, how long are rotating keys retained post-rotation?

3) BAA scope: HavenWell legal asked whether subprocessor notifications and a 30-day removal window are included in the BAA draft. Also asking for your standard indemnity language for PHI breaches.

4) Endpoint logging: we need a table of what logs include PHI, what is redacted, and retention windows by default (hosted vs dedicated).

Could you provide concise answers and any supporting artifacts (control matrices, redlines, diagrams) by EOD tomorrow? Attaching the excerpt of their RFP so it maps to your answers.

Appreciate it — Laura

--
Laura Jensen
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
HavenWell Health
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@havenwell.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-03T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on PHI dataflows and BAA terms for Redwood

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below and I attached three artifacts that map to each item (controls summary, BAA draft, updated dataflow diagram). I'll flag where we need legal input from our side.

1) Persistent storage: Hosted API routes may persist very short-lived KV cache items for streaming continuity (typical TTL < 60s) but we do not persist PHI to long-term blob/object storage for hosted customers by default. Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to persist request/response logs to customer-managed storage for debugging/retention; that is explicitly an opt-in setting.

2) Encryption at rest & keys: For Hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed keys by default (AWS KMS-backed). We also support BYOK via customer KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. Key rotation: managed keys rotate automatically every 90 days; rotated key material is not retained beyond 7 days after rotation unless a recovery window is requested during a rollout (we document that in the controls matrix).

3) BAA scope & subprocessors: Our standard BAA (attached) includes a subprocessor notification clause with a 30-day notice period and a removal process subject to technical feasibility; I highlighted that clause in the draft. Indemnity: our standard contract includes breach-limited indemnities tied to proven Redwood negligence; for customers requiring expanded indemnity we typically treat that as a contract negotiation point tied to an enterprise SLA commitment. I’ve flagged this for legal (cc Rishi).

4) Endpoint logging and PHI:
- Default hosted logging: request metadata (timestamps, request IDs), token counts, error traces — these logs do not include full request bodies or user-provided PHI.
- Optional debug logging (opt-in): request/response bodies can be captured for a 30-day window if enabled by customer; we recommend Dedicated/Private for production PHI capture.
- Retention: Hosted default logs retained 90 days; Dedicated customers can configure retention. Access control uses RBAC with audit trails.

Attachments: Redwood_HIPAA_Readiness_Summary_20270803.pdf (controls & SOC2 mapping), Redwood_BAA_Draft_20270803.docx (highlighted clauses), PHI_Dataflow_Diagram_v2.png

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the BAA redlines and the dataflow diagram. Samir / HavenWell Legal — are you available 11:00–12:00 PT? Rishi, Monica — can you join for the tech/legal walkthrough?

Best,
Hannah

• For the hosted TTL you mentioned (<60s) — can you confirm whether that KV cache can be configured to zero-retention for customers who want guaranteed non-persistence?
• On indemnity: our legal team will want to see the exact breach indemnity clause language in the BAA (we'll redline if needed). Can you confirm Redwood will accept an initial redline exchange via DocuSign?

If you can add a short table on the call that maps common RFP questions (PHI-at-rest, PHI-in-transit, subprocessor list, data residency) to the attached artifacts, that will speed review.

Samir/Laura — confirmed on the call at 11:30 PT. Quick answers ahead of our meeting:

• Zero-retention option: yes — Hosted customers can enable strict no-persistence mode which disables short-lived KV caching for their tenant (we call this "transient-only mode"). We'll share the config toggle and the audit events produced when it's enabled.

• BAA redlines via DocuSign: yes — we accept an initial redline exchange through DocuSign. I've included a DocuSign link in related_links and our Legal contact will handle the envelope. Rishi, please loop in Legal and prepare a brief talking deck on indemnity limits we typically accept.

For the call I will have: (1) a one-slide mapping table of RFP items -> artifacts (2) PHI Dataflow diagram (attached) (3) key lines in BAA to discuss (subprocessors, removal window, indemnity). Monica will run through logging/retention specifics. Aditya will cover KMS/BYOK technical integration.

See you tomorrow — Hannah

Director, Compliance Sales
